scout.purpose: Users expect to resume a screen after the system reclaims a background process, but restoration must reconstruct state without serialising the entire application.
scout.realWorldUse: Bundles, rememberSaveable or rememberSerializable, SavedStateHandle, and local storage cooperate to restore navigation, drafts, filters, and selected records.
scout.outcome: Classify state by lifetime and size, store minimal reconstruction data, and verify a true process-death restoration path.

sections.title: Memory, saved state, and persistence cover different lifetimes

blocks.text: ViewModel keeps complex screen state cheaply in memory across configuration recreation. Saved-state APIs serialise small values outside the process so a replacement can recover after system-initiated process death. Persistent storage keeps application data across process death, full screen dismissal, and device restart. Use them together: persist Note content, retain a loaded NotesUiState in ViewModel, and save only query text, selected note ID, or navigation key needed to reload. Saved state is not a database; large lists and bitmaps increase main-thread serialisation cost and risk transaction-size failures.

sections.title: SavedStateHandle belongs at ViewModel reconstruction boundaries

blocks.text: SavedStateHandle exposes key-based and observable saved values to a ViewModel created with the proper saved-state owner. Initial navigation arguments can seed it. Store stable, small, serialisable values and centralise keys or use typed helpers. A saved value written while a host is stopped may not be committed until a later start-stop cycle, so saved state is a system restoration facility rather than synchronous durable storage. Remove obsolete keys when a flow completes. If a process comes back from a deep link, navigation arguments and saved state can converge on the same explicit note identifier.

blocks.caption: The handle restores one stable identity; the repository remains the source of the full note.

blocks.title: Factory ownership matters
blocks.text: A manually constructed SavedStateHandle without the correct registry owner cannot provide real process-death restoration.

sections.title: Recreation is not the same experiment as process death

blocks.text: Rotation proves configuration recreation but usually retains the process and ViewModel, so it cannot validate saved-state recovery alone. To test system-initiated process death, place the activity in a restorable stopped state, terminate the process using supported developer tooling without force-stopping the package, then return through recents or the original entry. Force stop changes package state and blocks normal launch paths until user action, so it represents a different scenario. Also test explicit Back: the user dismissed that destination and usually should not receive its saved instance state. Record expected state for rotation, background process recreation, Back, task removal, and fresh launch.

inspect.title: Review an oversized saved state
inspect.code:
savedStateHandle["allNotes"] = notes // 4,000 rich note objects
savedStateHandle["selectedId"] = selected.id
walkthrough: The full list duplicates durable data and requires expensive main-thread serialisation.
The selected ID is a small reconstruction key.
After recreation, the repository can reload notes and apply the selected ID.
inspect.expectedOutput: Remove allNotes from saved state; persist notes and retain only identifiers and small UI inputs.

trap_check.mistake: Putting complete domain collections into a Bundle or SavedStateHandle.
trap_check.why: Serialisation is limited, main-thread work grows, and durable data is duplicated.
trap_check.fix: Persist domain data and save minimal keys needed to reload it.

trap_check.mistake: Testing only rotation and declaring process restoration complete.
trap_check.why: Rotation normally preserves ViewModel and process memory.
trap_check.fix: Run a distinct stopped-process recreation scenario and verify repository reload.

challenge_intro.task: Implement selected-note and query restoration using SavedStateHandle plus a persistent repository, then test rotation, stopped-process recreation, Back, and fresh launch.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: Only small reconstruction values enter saved state. Full notes reload from durable storage. Expected behaviour is documented separately for all four scenarios.

recall.answer: Small values required to reconstruct UI, such as IDs, query text, or navigation keys.
ViewModel itself does not survive system-initiated process death.

recall.prompt: Does Back normally preserve a dismissed destination?
recall.answer: No, explicit dismissal usually removes that screen and its saved-state expectation.

objectives: Choose among ViewModel, saved state, and persistence.
